test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-5) Official Paper (Held On: 15 June 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A and B together can do a piece of work in 10 days. If A alone can do the same work in 15 days and C alone can do the same work in 20 days, then in how many days can B and C together do the same work?
solution:
**Given:**

A and B together can do a piece of work in 10 days

A alone can do the same work in 15 days

C alone can do the same work in 20 days

**Calculations:**

According to the question,

⇒ One day work of (A) = 1/15

⇒ One day work of (C) = 1/20

Let the no. of days B alone took to complete the work be 'x'

⇒ One day work of (B) = 1/x

Now A's one-day work + B's one-day work = (A + B) one-day work

⇒ (A) + (B) = (A + B) 

⇒ (1/15) + (1/x) = (1/10)

⇒ (1/x) = (1/10) - (1/15) 

⇒ (1/x) = (15 - 10)/150

⇒ (1/x) = 5/150 

⇒ (1/x) = 1/30 = 30 days

B alone can do the same work in 30 days

Now the work done by B and C together,

B's one-day work + C's one-day work = (B + C) one-day work

⇒ (1/30) + (1/20) = 1/(B + C)

⇒ (2 + 3)/60 = 1/(B + C)

⇒ 5/60 = 1/(B + C)

⇒ 1/(B + C) = 1/12

⇒ (B + C) = 12 days

**∴ B and C together do the same work in 12 days.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**

The total work = LCM(15, 20, 10) = 60 units (since the work is the same for all).

Efficiency of A = 60 / 15 = 4 units/day

Efficiency of A and B together = Total work / Time taken = 60 / 10 = 6 units/day

Efficiency of B = Efficiency of A and B together - Efficiency of A = 6 - 4 = 2 units/day

Efficiency of C = 60 / 20 = 3 units/day

Combined efficiency of B and C = Efficiency of B + Efficiency of C = 2 + 3 = 5 units/day

Time taken = Total work / Combined efficiency = 60 / 5 = 12 days

**∴ B and C together can complete the work in 12 days.**
